rv.q: Michael Longhurst’s pitch-perfect revival is now being offered up to a much wider demographic.
And a show I once described as 'too good to be good' grows into the titanic dimensions of greatness.
This is the brilliance of the show: Kushner burrows down into just two households, at a moment of huge global political change, to explore the realities of how change really comes about.
Moment by moment, the show offers a stunning experience, but overall it comes across as stylistically and dramatically unbalanced.
Not only is Clarke phenomenal with her voice and performance as Caroline but the show's themes around economic inequality are as urgent today as ever.
Clarke gives a superlative performance that catches both Caroline's melancholy at being ground down by poverty and her anger at the realisation she is trapped in it for ever.

Caroline or Change has a lot going for it and three potentially interesting plot lines that should fully engage, yet it never quite unites as tidily and explosively as it promises to do, the wackier aspects serving to alienate rather than enhance the rest of the story.

cn.t: Critics largely rave over this Kushner-Tesori musical, with Sharon D Clarke's powerhouse performance drawing particular acclaim. A profound, moving work that earns near-universal praise.

vr.q: This is a 5-star musical I can only give this presentation a very good four stars
